audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer reads Yone/Skill/Skill/Skill/Yone/Skill/Yone while the content layer and the packet both read Katarina/Yone/Katarina/Katarina/Katarina/Yone/Katarina. Five rows disagree outright, including level 6 where full says Yone and content says Katarina.
audit.why: The content whys are grounded and match the 54.05% win rate: Yone has no hard CC before 6 beyond a two-stack Mortal Steel he has to charge, and his single power window is the first-item duel.
audit.corrected: All seven full-layer sides moved to the content values with whys and ratings rewritten to match.

audit.why: spikes[] correctly identify 3-5 as yours, first item as his duel window, and late as yours. Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 against your 75s Death Lotus, and Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 dropping to 10s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is stated loosely: Soul Unbound is his engage AND his return path, so the snapback is forced — but the page never says the return is involuntary or gives its cooldown. Spirit Cleave's shield scaling (bigger the more champions it hits) is never mentioned either.
audit.why: enemyKit E text says his spirit is FORCED back to his body when the ability ends; enemyKit W text says the shield value increases with the number of champions hit and that its cooldown scales with attack speed.
audit.corrected: Both stated, with the 22-second rank-1 E cooldown as the fight timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digit (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d invents a 'fifteen-second' Soul Unbound window.
audit.why: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5; Mortal Steel is a flat 4s; Spirit Cleave is 14s before attack speed; Fate Sealed is 120/100/80.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d is tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d is tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED). The packet also flags three fabricated names: 'Bouncing Blades' for Katarina's Q in spikes[0] and early, and a 'Preparation' reset that is not in her kit.
audit.why: Riot's text for Katarina's Q in the kit file carries no ability name at all, and there is no ability called Preparation anywhere in her kit.
audit.corrected: Bullets rewritten to their titles; fabricated names replaced with the mechanic and the real Shunpo/Dagger wording.

edits.before: Q the wave and collect the dagger — every pickup is a free spin; the lane learns your dagger geometry or bleeds.
edits.after: Your 625-range Dagger outreaches a 450 Mortal Steel, and he has no shield or tornado yet. Chip him every time he steps up to last-hit.

edits.after: He hits 2 first off the melee wave, and Mortal Steel into Spirit Cleave with the shield up beats anything your half-kit has. Give a wave.

edits.before: Full kit: E to daggers, not faces — the blink economy is the champion; trade only through steel on the ground.
edits.after: He has no hard CC until 6 beyond a tornado he must charge. Blink to a Dagger behind him, trade, and leave before the second Q stack.

edits.before: Dagger-trade on cooldown: Q-E-W-E strings chunk and the resets... wait for kills. Bank the patterns.

edits.before: Death Lotus online — any 2v2 near your daggers is a blender invoice. The reset engine is armed.
edits.after: Soul Unbound is both his entry and his only exit, and the return is forced. Spin on the snapback and he has nowhere to be.

edits.before: First item spike: full dagger strings delete squishies and one kill opens the chain reaction.
edits.after: His first item is a duel spike: shield plus lifesteal outlasts one rotation of yours. Do not coinflip — shove and cash the wave elsewhere.

edits.before: Late Kata is a chain reaction: enter on daggers, lotus the clump, reset through the wreckage, repeat until silence.
edits.after: He must commit first with E or a 1000-range Fate Sealed. The moment he does, flank the fight and reset through his backline.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. It governs your forward steps. - E Shunpo (second use) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 and 10s maxed. It is his entry and his exit both, and the snap back to his body is forced, not chosen — that return is your window. - Spirit Cleave is 14s and shields more the more champions it hits; never open into a fresh one. - Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 against your 75s.

edits.after: Fight on the snapback, not the entry

edits.before: His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.

edits.before: Yone burns Soul Unbound on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.

edits.before: That is Yone’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: His only pre-6 interrupt is the two-stack Mortal Steel knock-up. Count his Q casts and start the spin on an empty stack, not a loaded one.

edits.before: Your lotus dies to one interrupt — counting their CC before spinning is the entire skill floor of the champion.
edits.after: A 4-second Q and a shield that rebuilds every 14 mean he wins any fight that lasts. Chunk and leave; never settle in for a melee war.

edits.before: Shunpo onto a face with the CC still loaded — Katarina dies to held buttons, not skill, and everyone holding one knows it.

edits.before: Ahead, chain it: zone Yone off daggers, lotus every skirmish, and reset through the map — fed Katarina is a weather event.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the duel spike: shove, roam, and take objectives so his first item arrives late. He needs gold to win the format he wants.

edits.before: Carry through chain reactions — one kill is three; your job is the first domino and the discipline to wait for it.
edits.after: Carry off his commitment. Every Yone fight opens with Soul Unbound or Fate Sealed; you enter second, onto the spot his body is waiting in.

edits.before: If Yone gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Soul Unbound extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q bounces and stay relevant through reset potential.
edits.after: A fed Yone reaches the shield-and-lifesteal duel spike early, which is the one phase that is genuinely his. Farm from Dagger range, never contest a wave he is standing on, and wait for a fight where he has already spent his 22-second E.

edits.before: You are the cleanup that starts fights: enter on steel, lotus the clump, reset through the kill, and exit through the panic.
edits.after: You clean up after his entry: he blinks behind the back line with Fate Sealed and pulls, and that is the moment his exit is already spent.

edits.before: With Q-W-E online you can Bouncing Blades a dagger behind him, Shunpo to it, and Preparation-reset out before his Mortal Steel tornado charges. Yone has no hard CC pre-6, so short trades onto dagger pickups win — just don't stand in the wave when his W Spirit Cleave shield is up.
edits.after: With Q-W-E online you can land a Dagger behind him, Shunpo to it, and step out before his Mortal Steel tornado charges. Yone has no hard CC pre-6, so short trades onto dagger pickups win — just don't stand in the wave when his 14-second Spirit Cleave shield is up.

edits.before: Level 1 your Bouncing Blades poke and dagger pickups outdamage his Q stacking — chip him when he steps up to last-hit, but respect level 2: he hits it first off the melee wave and a Mortal Steel plus W trade with shield up beats anything you have. Give one wave of room at 2, then re-engage at 3.
edits.after: Level 1 your 625-range Dagger poke and pickups outdamage his 450-range Q stacking — chip him when he steps up to last-hit, but respect level 2: he hits it first off the melee wave and a Mortal Steel plus W trade with shield up beats anything you have. Give one wave of room at 2, then re-engage at 3.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 you control the lane: dagger-Shunpo in, E out before his Q3 tornado is charged, and never trade into an active Spirit Cleave shield. At 6 you win the all-in if his E is down or already cast — Death Lotus during his snapback window is a kill, since Fate Sealed's long windup gives you the first full rotation. Track his E on a 22-second early cooldown and force fights inside it; if he's playing safe, shove and hit his jungler's raptors or roam bot at 6.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 you control the lane: dagger-Shunpo in, blink out before his second Q stack charges, and never trade into an active Spirit Cleave shield. At 6 you win the all-in if his E is down or already cast — his spirit is forced back to the body it left, so you know the exact tile he returns to and can be standing on it. Track Soul Unbound on its 22-second rank-1 cooldown and force fights inside it; if he's playing safe, shove and take his raptors or roam bot at 6.

edits.before: At 6 Death Lotus wins the all-in because Yone's E snapback and slow Fate Sealed windup hand Kat the first full rotation.
edits.after: At 6 the forced Soul Unbound snapback tells you where he lands, and his 120-second R hands you the first rotation.

edits.after: Extended trades where a 14-second Spirit Cleave shield and lifesteal outlast your rotation

notes: Five of seven level-chart rows disagreed between layers; all seven full-layer sides moved to the content values as one atomic group with matching whys. No content win[N] edits were needed — that layer already matched the packet. Killed the fabricated names the packet flagged: 'Bouncing Blades' (Riot's text gives Katarina's Q no name in the kit file, so I wrote the mechanic and the 625 range) and 'Preparation', which is not an ability in her kit at all. Surfaced two things the page never stated: Soul Unbound's return is FORCED, so the tile he reappears on is known in advance, and Spirit Cleave's shield scales with the number of champions it hits. IMPORTANT for the QA pass: this brief's missingInteractions entry claims Katarina's Q grounds Yone's Mortal Steel and Fate Sealed. That comes from a derived 'grounding' flag on her Q, but Riot's own description of the ability says only that it throws a Dagger that bounces and lands — no grounding, no dash denial. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and did NOT write that interaction anywhere. It would be the strongest line in the matchup if true, so it needs a decision. Left unverified: the Immortal Shieldbow / Blade of the Ruined King item names in spikes[2] and late — item builds are not in the kit data. | COHERENCE: 2 chart edit(s) withdrawn — they moved the row to the enemy while leaving the phase why describing the owner winning it. Chart authority is an open question, so the label was reverted rather than the prose rewritten. Re-propose only as a side+why pair.
